# Vendored crates

**gpui-pre-windows** is GPUI's Windows platform at 0.3.12, from crates.io, under its Apache-2.0 licence. Four changes are made, marked `loom:`. The third, in `src/shaders.hlsl`, draws a rotated image, and the fourth, `load_pan_cursor` in `src/util.rs`, shows the system's pan cursors; both are described with **gpui-pre** below.

In `src/platform.rs`, the vsync thread only tells windows that are on screen to paint. Before the change it told every window to paint at every vblank, so the app's main thread woke 240 times a second while minimised, which cost 68–90 ms of CPU a second. Once every window has been off screen for a second, as when loom is in the tray, the thread looks five times a second rather than at every vblank. It waits that second because a window that's opening isn't on screen until its first frame, and the frames after that wait on this thread: without the wait, the chat showed up to 200 ms later at start.

A window on screen is told to paint only when it has something new to draw (`FrameDemand` in `src/window.rs`): GPUI says so through the window's `frame_waker` and `schedule_frame`, as it does for macOS's display link. A window shown and idle used to be woken at every vblank to find it had nothing to draw, 28–42 ms of CPU a second. While a touchpad gesture runs it's still told at every vblank, since Direct Manipulation is pumped from each paint (`src/direct_manipulation.rs`), and every window is told four times a second regardless, in case a frame GPUI put off isn't asked for again.

To move to a newer GPUI, copy that version's crate here and make the same changes again. If upstream has made them already, drop the patch from `../Cargo.toml` instead.

**gpui-base** is GPUI Base at 0.10.0, from crates.io, under its Apache-2.0 licence. Two changes are made, marked `loom:`. An inline `<span style="color: #rrggbb; font-weight: 500">` in Markdown gives its text that color and weight (`TextMark`'s `color` and `weight` in `src/text/node.rs`, read in `src/text/format/markdown.rs`). The chat draws an agent's name that way where a message mentions it, in the agent's colour. And a link whose text has its own colour keeps it, with no underline (`decorate_link` in `src/text/node.rs`), and under the pointer has a light background of that colour (`Inline::paint_link_hover` in `src/text/inline.rs`), so an agent's name is a link to its chat that still reads as the agent. To move to a newer GPUI Base, copy that version's crate here and make the same changes again, or drop the patch if upstream has a way to colour a span and a link.

**gpui-pre** is GPUI at 0.3.12, with its renderers **gpui-pre-apple** (Metal) and **gpui-pre-wgpu** (Linux), from crates.io, under their Apache-2.0 licence. Two changes are made, marked `loom:`. The first, across them and the Windows renderer above: an image can be drawn moved by a `TransformationMatrix`, as an SVG icon already could, so the chat can tilt a message's pictures. `PolychromeSprite` gains a `transformation` as its last field (`src/scene.rs`), which `Window::paint_image_transformed` sets (`src/window.rs`); `paint_image` and emoji pass the unit matrix. `TransformationMatrix::rotation_about` builds a rotation about a point, and `Transformation::into_matrix` (`src/elements/svg.rs`) is public. A moved image is culled and ordered against other primitives by the box around its moved corners. Each renderer's polychrome sprite shader (`shaders.hlsl`, `shaders.metal`, `shaders.wgsl` with its WebGL loader in `shaders_webgl.wgsl`) places the corners with the matrix, as the monochrome one does, and rounds the corners in the image's own space rather than on screen. A moved image's quad is a pixel larger each way, sampling the tile's edge there, so its edges are smoothed on both sides. An image that isn't moved takes the same path as before and is drawn to the bit as it was. gpui-pre-apple builds its shader structs from its own copy of GPUI's sources in `vendor/gpui`, so `scene.rs`, `window.rs` and `platform.rs` there are kept the same as gpui-pre's. To move to a newer GPUI, copy that version's crates here and make the same changes again, or drop the patches if upstream can draw a transformed image and show pan cursors.

The second change, also marked `loom:`, shows the cursors of a browser's middle-button scrolling. `PanCursor` (`src/platform.rs`) is up and down at rest, up, or down. `Window::set_pan_cursor` shows one over the whole window, ahead of every `CursorStyle`, until it's set to `None`, and isn't part of a frame, so it shows at once. `Window::hovered_cursor_style` gives the cursor style under the pointer, which loom reads so the middle button leaves links and buttons alone. They aren't `CursorStyle` variants because every platform matches `CursorStyle` whole, so gpui-pre-linux and gpui-pre-web would have to be vendored too. Instead, `Platform::set_pan_cursor` defaults to the nearest resize cursor, and Windows and the Mac draw their own. Windows (above) loads user32's pan cursors, resources without names: 32652 at rest, 32655 up, 32656 down. The Mac has none, so **gpui-pre-macos** draws them.

**gpui-pre-macos** is GPUI's macOS platform at 0.3.12, from crates.io, under its Apache-2.0 licence. One change is made, marked `loom:`: `set_pan_cursor` shows a pan cursor through the window's cursor rects, as `set_cursor_style` shows a style. `src/pan_cursor.rs` draws each the way Windows draws its own, black triangles and a dot with a 1-point white edge on a 32-point square, into an image with a 1× and a 2× bitmap, and makes the `NSCursor` once. Its tests don't build, as upstream's didn't, without GPUI's test support. To move to a newer GPUI, copy that version's crate here and make the same change again.
